column1: # The Handbook spelling converter's oracle (tunatale-h0q3.38), checked against the committed
# wolff_lexicon.json.gz by tests/test_ceb_lexicon_spellings.py: the lexicon writes KEEP and never REJECT.
# Rows: every word the h0q3.38 rebuild changed, and every word a whole-word-count build would have
# changed but should not. Settled by the owner's rule "if the corpus agrees, follow the corpus"
# (2026-11-04), counts from cebuano_surface_frequency.tsv.gz (whole words) and cebuano_frequency.tsv.gz
#   corpus        whole words: KEEP written >= 5 times and >= 2x REJECT
#   corpus-root   the word's root as writers spell it (as a word, else by lemma)
#   follows-root  the corpus is silent or split on the word; written as its root is
#   other-word    the count belongs to another word (a name, a homograph): VOWEL_OVERRIDES
#   kept          the corpus cannot tell (homograph or unattested): the build before h0q3.38's spelling
#   rule          the corpus splits; the Raisanen rule decides
#   neutral       the corpus splits and both spellings are fine
#   residual      KEEP is wrong, REJECT right: a known miss, explained. Fixing it turns this test red; flip the row.
